provenance_note: Every ref in this artifact was derived from SPEC-bidevaluation and the cited sources by a separate agent with no access to this page, and every got was recomputed in the browser by the same functions the interface calls; no stored result is reused.
reference: Hand-built evaluation states in the tool-neutral vocabulary of SPEC-bidevaluation §13.1 (the §3.1 state object, optionally with a project-package document and a load/write action), covering the four §9 presets with their printed figures, every rule of the §5 table with at least one triggering case and one case that lists it absent, the boundary behaviour the spec states for the two thresholds (BID-R-031 fires on a strict '<' and BID-R-032 on a strict '>', so the exactly-equal cases are near-misses and use values that are exact in binary floating point), the degenerate weight geometries (a single row with omega_k = 1, zero-weight rows, a zero-weight row as the only critical one, dominance with x_crit = 100 %), ties at rank 1 and inside lower ranks, an edit of the published scoring table that reverses a rank, the two and ten bidder limits with their one-over near-misses, the §3.3 id derivations, the TQ drafts of §4.8 with their ids and default templates, and the package integration of §7 (explicit load, read mapping, ignored sections, an unknown top-level key, flags including an orphan, the write that replaces one item and leaves the others byte-identical, the collision and id-pattern refusals, and a write/resume round trip). Expected values were derived from the spec clause by clause and computed with an own standard-library Python implementation of §3.3 and §4.2-§4.8 (bidevaluation-ref.py beside this corpus, which regenerates this file and re-verifies every value against it); the sensitivity arithmetic is additionally checked against explicit 2^n vertex enumeration of the weight box and against the algebra of Triantaphyllou & Sanchez (1997) relation (8a). The external references are process context only: ISO 10845-1:2020 and Directive 2014/24/EU prescribe none of the numbers here, and no case claims conformity with either.
reference_citations: ISO 10845-1:2020 Construction procurement — Part 1: Processes, methods and procedures. Verified 2026-09-22 from the ISO/DIS 10845-1 sample (cdn.standards.iteh.ai/samples/72467/) and the ISO catalogue entry iso.org/standard/72467: clause 6.7 'Tender process and procedures', clause 6.8 'Award of contracts', Annex F (informative) 'Standard selection methods', definition 3.27 'quality' = 'totality of features and characteristics of a product or service that bears on the ability of the product or service to satisfy stated or implied needs'. The content of the evaluation methods is not in the verified extract, so no case in this corpus derives a number from the standard.

Directive 2014/24/EU of 26 February 2014 on public procurement (CELEX 32014L0024). Verified 2026-09-22 from legislation.gov.uk/eudr/2014/24/article/56 and .../article/67: art. 56(1)(a) 'the tender complies with the requirements, conditions and criteria set out in the contract notice ... and in the procurement documents'; art. 56(3) contracting authorities 'may ... request the economic operators concerned to submit, supplement, clarify or complete the relevant information or documentation within an appropriate time limit ... in full compliance with the principles of equal treatment and transparency'; art. 67(2) MEAT 'shall be identified on the basis of the price or cost ... and may include the best price-quality ratio'; art. 67(4) award criteria 'shall be accompanied by specifications that allow the information provided by the tenderers to be effectively verified'; art. 67(5) the relative weighting is specified in the procurement documents. Context only: this tool computes no price and is not a MEAT calculator (spec §2 item 1).

E. Triantaphyllou, A. Sánchez, 'A sensitivity analysis approach for some deterministic multi-criteria decision-making methods', Decision Sciences 28(1), 1997, 151-194. Bibliographic record verified 2026-09-22 from Crossref (doi 10.1111/j.1540-5915.1997.tb01306.x); the full text is paywalled, so the paper's printed Tables 2-5 are not re-read here and no case checks them. What is checked is the algebra the spec relies on: relation (8a) delta_{k,i,j} = (P_j - P_i)/(a_jk - a_ik), the relative form (6), and the 'robust criterion' notion.
Own reference implementation: bidevaluation-ref.py beside this corpus (standard library only; --spec reproduces every figure printed in spec §4.7 and §9.1-§9.4).
tolerance: Categorical outputs (verdict, sensitive, rule membership, finding counts, rank, knock-out state, provisional, challenger ids, draft ids and kinds, derived evaluation id, package_written, ignored sections) are exact: they are enumerations, integers, booleans or strings, and any difference is a logic difference. Numeric tolerances are taken from the arithmetic, not chosen to pass. score_pct and margin_pp: abs 1e-9 pp — §4.3 is a finite sum of products of user decimals, so only floating-point rounding separates two correct implementations (spec §13.2). delta_pp, critical_change_pp, x_crit_pct, pair_t_pct and r_pct: abs 1e-6 — each is a quotient of two float sums (§4.5 x* = -D_0/D_1 after two divisions by 1 - omega_k; §4.6 t_j = sum w d / sum w |d|), where a different but equally valid order of operations can move the last few ulps; 1e-6 is far below the 1e-4 printed rounding the spec's own acceptance criterion 5 uses and far above the ~1e-13 relative error the expressions can accumulate at these magnitudes. The two threshold boundaries are handled as spec §13.2 requires: the equality cases use dyadic values (|delta*| = 12.5 pp against threshold_pp 12.5; x_crit = 50 % against x_pct 50) that are exact in binary floating point, so the strict comparison is decided without tolerance.
reference_author_note: independent reference authored without access to the tool code
coverage: 95 cases. Every rule of the §5 table (50 rules) has at least one case whose trigger fires it and at least one case that lists it in rules_absent; dedicated near-misses sit one step from the trigger for BID-R-002 (ten bidders), BID-R-003 (a 16-character id against a 17-character one), BID-R-005 (150 rows against 151), BID-R-006 (weight 0 against a negative weight), BID-R-008 (values 10 and 0 against 10.5 and all-zero), BID-R-018 (the same missing cell with its clarification open), BID-R-031 and BID-R-032 (the exact-equality boundaries), BID-R-066 (a flag on a requirement outside the evaluation) and BID-R-069 (same id, same requisition). Headline claims: the four presets of §9 with the scores, ranks, knock-outs, per-row sensitivity table, t_j values, x_crit and verdict printed in §4.7 and §9.1-§9.4. Boundaries: 2 and 10 bidders, 1 and 150 rows, id lengths 16 (admissible) and 17 (one over), scoring-table values 0 and 10, omega_k = 1, zero weights, score ties at rank 1 and at a lower rank, |delta*| exactly at threshold_pp, x_pct exactly at x_crit, x_crit = 0 and x_crit = 100, and a scoring table whose maximum is 5 rather than 10. Disputable checks carry "disputable": true with the reason in the case note. Seven cases and two fixture corrections were added by adjudication 2026-09-23 and say so in their notes: the four of the second pass cover an absent cells[] pair, the two default TQ templates of §4.8, cell fields kept outside their own status, and a row id outside the advisory local pattern of §3.2. | A1 §5 says BID-R-001..008 'stop the computation' without saying whether the cell-level findings are still listed; cases with verdict INVALID therefore check the verdict and the fired blocker only. | A2 BID-R-003 'equals another bidder id' does not say whether both duplicates are targets or only the later one (case r003-duplicate-bidder-id follows the symmetric reading and is marked disputable). | A3 The length half of BID-R-005 (>150 rows) names the field requirements[i].id but triggers on the array; this reference fires one instance targeted at 'requirements' (case r005-151-rows, disputable). | A4 BID-R-008 names the field scoring_table, so this reference fires one instance per evaluation however many values are bad; a reading of one instance per offending key is also open. No case here has more than one bad value, so nothing turns on it. | A5 §4.4 defined the leader only when |L*| = 1 and the margin 'when |Q| >= 2'. Closed by adjudication 2026-09-23 in favour of this reference: with a tie at the top leader and margin_pp are null, while delta* = 0, x_crit = 0 and rank1_stable = (x_pct <= 0) are still reported as §4.5/§4.6 require; SPEC §4.4 carries the clarification in its changelog. | A6 BID-R-033 fires when 'every row robust (delta* undefined)'; a row reported n/a for omega_k = 1 is not called robust by §4.5. Closed by adjudication 2026-09-23 on the parenthesis: the trigger is delta* undefined, so an all-n/a table fires it (case omega-one-single-row, which keeps its disputable mark because the rule text alone still admits the other reading). | A7 §7.2 step 5 reports 'sections ignored by the runtime (everything outside reads)'. Closed by adjudication 2026-09-23 against the earlier literal reading: provenance is a top-level envelope key (PKG §2, §2.4) that the runtime hands to the tool rather than dropping, and the spec's place for a key that arrives unused is the 'fields read but not used' list, so ignored_sections names sections only; SPEC §7.2 step 5 carries the clarification in its changelog. | A8 §7.4 carries evaluated_at as an RFC 3339 timestamp, but the §3.1 state holds only evaluation.evaluation_date (a date) and selection.selected_at; the source of evaluated_at is not stated and is not benchmarked. | A9 BID-R-066 needs flag kinds 'requisition' and 'bid_evaluation', which the closed target_kind list of PKG §2.3 does not contain; the fixtures here assume the list is extended by the new registers. | A10 §4.6 heads its derivation with '|L*| = 1' but defines the pairwise output over every ordered qualified pair; this reference emits pair_t_pct whenever |Q| >= 2 and x_crit only when the leader is unique. | A11 Spec open question Q1: the requisition register carries no class or weight, so the package fixtures supply the proposed requirement_terms[]; a requisition without it defaults every row to mandatory, weight 1.

not_benchmarked.Corpus limitation 1: Whether an evaluator's classification of a bid answer (compliant, deviation, missing, not applicable, exceeds) is right: engineering judgement, no reference exists (spec §14).
not_benchmarked.Corpus limitation 2: ISO 10845-1 evaluation methods and scoring schedules: the verified extract (ISO/DIS sample plus catalogue entry) stops at the table of contents and definitions, so no case claims conformity or derives a number from the standard (spec §14).
not_benchmarked.Corpus limitation 3: Commercial evaluation, price, life-cycle cost and any MEAT combination: outside the tool by spec §2 item 1.
not_benchmarked.Corpus limitation 4: The printed numerical tables of Triantaphyllou & Sánchez (1997) (their Tables 2-5 and the dropped digit the spec §4.9 reports in the A2-A3/C3 entry): the full text is paywalled here. Case literature-triantaphyllou-sanchez-equivalence checks the algebraic identity between relation (8a) and §4.5 instead.
not_benchmarked.Corpus limitation 5: Which non-blocker findings, if any, are reported alongside verdict INVALID: §5 says BID-R-001..008 'stop the computation' without saying whether the cell-level findings are still listed. Cases whose verdict is INVALID therefore check the verdict and the presence of the blocker only, never finding_counts or rules_absent.
not_benchmarked.Corpus limitation 6: Seven-language wording of the UI, the TQ default templates outside English, the report profile layout and the figures F1/F2: QA, not benchmark (spec §14).
not_benchmarked.Corpus limitation 7: Permalink encoding, the >4 kB permalink notice, CSV column formatting and the 'Copy for deviationregister' payload: transport, checked in QA.
not_benchmarked.Corpus limitation 8: written_item.evaluated_at: §7.4 shows an RFC 3339 timestamp, but the §3.1 state carries only evaluation.evaluation_date (a date) and selection.selected_at, and the spec does not say which one feeds it (ambiguity A8).
not_benchmarked.Corpus limitation 9: The ±x box at a sampled rather than exhaustive enumeration: §4.6 is solved in closed form here and cross-checked against explicit 2^n enumeration for n ≤ 12, so no sampling tolerance is needed or benchmarked.

adapter.note: Each case state is normalised with normState() and evaluated with evaluate(), the function the interface calls; package cases write the fixture into localStorage, read it through DiagramProject, and restore the store afterwards. rules_present is graded as containment and rules_absent as exclusion, which together are set equality over the 50 rules of SPEC 5; rule_instances targets are compared as sets.
